artboards.title: Home on a phone, in dark
Nothing needs you, and the first run
The morning summary and urgent emails

annotations.text:
HandsFreeOS Milestone 8, step 0: the Action Center. Home becomes one ranked list of what needs attention, with the dollars affected at the top. Same look as Milestones 1 to 7. There are eight kinds: hot lead, unanswered lead, gone quiet, no next action, not confirmed, approval, customer waiting and overdue task. Every card has Handle, Let HandsFreeOS Handle, and ⋯ for Assign, Snooze and Dismiss, with Undo. Only two things run on their own: asking customers to confirm, and one follow-up for a lead that went quiet. The follow-up stays off until an owner reads the wording.
Try: Main and Home in dark (Mine and Everyone; ⋯ on a card, then Snooze or Dismiss, then Undo; Show all 4; Handled by HandsFreeOS; Cancel under Coming up; Approve on Angela) and Settings (the switches, and Looks good, turn on).

Sample data only: Lone Star HVAC & Roofing, the same fictional Houston business as Milestones 5 to 7. Home and the urgent email are Tuesday, September 22, 8:05 AM Central Time. The morning email is 7:00 AM, Let HandsFreeOS Handle is 9:40 AM, Confirm is 4:30 PM and the empty Home is 4:45 PM. The team is Dale (owner), Priya (admin) and Marco (member). Ava is the AI teammate, with 17 of 20 approved.
$47,300 affected = Maria Lopez $18,500 + Tom Reyes $12,400 + Linda Okafor $9,800 + Riverside Apartments $6,600. Leads without a value show “About $4,200” and aren’t counted. Dale’s Mine view is $40,700 and 5 items. People, numbers, prices and addresses are placeholders.

For you to decide on this canvas:
1. The kind names on the cards: Hot lead, Unanswered lead, Gone quiet, No next action, Not confirmed, Approval, Customer waiting, Overdue task.
2. The follow-up wording and its preview (Settings), and the reminder’s “Reply C to confirm.”
3. The defaults: a hot lead after 10 minutes or $5,000, unanswered after 15 open-hours minutes, gone quiet after 7 days (2 for New, 14 for Due), the 48-hour window, and a $4,200 typical job value.
4. The dismiss reasons: Already taken care of, Not a real lead, They’re not interested, Something else.
5. Whether “Email me when something is urgent” replaces “Email me when a customer is waiting” in Settings, Account, as drawn on Emails.
6. What Let HandsFreeOS Handle does for a hot lead. The plan says it asks first and means a call. Here it gets the call ready, since HandsFreeOS can’t make the call for you.

Choices I made that the plan didn’t spell out:
• The business is Lone Star HVAC & Roofing, as on the Milestone 5 to 7 boards and in the seed.
• Home’s times follow 8:05 AM, so Coming up says “Will follow up at 9:05 · Cancel”. The 10:40 example is on Let HandsFreeOS Handle, at 9:40 AM.
• The morning email is written at 7:00 AM, so it has Dale’s 3 items from then, not Home’s 9.
• A group counts each of its items: 9 = 2 urgent + 3 cards + a group of 4.
• Tom Reyes stays on the list because HandsFreeOS followed up on Sep 13, and it waits 14 days before another.
• Approvals and overdue tasks show Let HandsFreeOS Handle turned off, since it can’t do them.
• On a phone, the snooze choices sit right in the ⋯ sheet, and Today and Coming up fold into rows below the list.
• The Settings tab is called Action Center and sits last. It shows follow-ups “Off until an owner reads the wording”, while Home shows them on.
• A new business (Northstar Electric) keeps the setup checklist, plus a short word about what Home becomes.
